title: Model Activation: Launch Runbook & Cross-functional Checklist
creator: Marina Alvarez
description: This runbook coordinates the cross-functional steps to add a new model variant to the Redwood catalog and go-to-market. It covers catalog metadata, performance benchmarks, release notes, docs, SDK examples, marketing assets, and the staged rollout plan. Use this document to track owners, blockers, and launch tasks for each area.
checklist: Catalog entry: Publish model card with name, tags, architecture, compatible runtimes, quantization support, cost-per-token estimates, and sample outputs (owner: PM)
Model artifacts: Ensure model binaries, conversion artifacts, and checksum are stored in model registry with access controls (owner: ENG)
Benchmarks: Run standardized latency and throughput tests (p50/p95/p99) across supported instance types; attach raw results and summary (owner: Research)
Quality checks: Run evaluation suite on standard prompt sets and policy filters; compare to baseline and record regression warnings (owner: Applied ML)
Compatibility matrix: Validate model with SDK versions, streaming API, function calling, and structured output features (owner: SDK/Platform)
Docs: Create Getting Started guide, SDK snippets (Python/Node), code examples for streaming and function calls, and integration notes for Dedicated/Private deployments (owner: DX/Docs)
Release notes: Draft user-facing release notes with breaking changes, known limitations, recommended fallback models, and upgrade guidance (owner: PM)
Design assets: Prepare catalog thumbnail, architecture diagram, and comparison table if promoting as a recommended model (owner: Design)
Pricing & billing: Confirm token pricing entry, billing SKU, and quota defaults; coordinate with Finance to map to pricing plans (owner: Finance/PM)
Console: Add per-model dashboard filters, default alert thresholds, and trace sampling config (owner: Console)
Observability: Ensure token-level cost, latency, error breakdowns, and sample traces are surfaced for the new model (owner: SRE/Observability)
Security & compliance: Complete security review, KMS key policy check, and log retention settings for Private deployments; file security sign-off (owner: Security)
Legal/Policy: Validate license compatibility of the model files and include attributions in the model card (owner: Legal)
SDK releases: Publish patch release with model name added to model enums, update changelog, and link SDK documentation (owner: SDK)
Samples & reference app: Add example app demonstrating typical latency/cost tradeoffs and a scripted benchmark harness (owner: Solutions Engineering)
Customer comms: Prepare email segment drafts, account-level in-product banners, and support FAQ (owner: Growth/Support)
Marketing: Draft blog post outline, social creative, and partner announcement schedule; sync embargo times with PR (owner: Marketing)
Canary rollout: Define canary cohort size, monitoring criteria, and automatic rollback thresholds (owner: Platform Release Lead)
Support readiness: Create triage runbook for common issues and run internal support training session (owner: Support)
Post-launch metrics: Define initial KPIs (activation rate, latency by percentile, cost per 1k tokens, regression alerts) and dashboard links (owner: PM/Analytics)
Post-mortem plan: Schedule 2-week and 6-week reviews to capture adoption, quality regressions, and follow-up work (owner: PM)
Localization: If applicable, prepare localized examples and double-check any region-specific compliance notes (owner: Intl Program)
Final signoffs: Collect approvals from ENG, Security, Legal, Design, and Marketing before public listing (owner: PM)
Fallback configuration: Register fallback model mapping in smart routing policy and document behavior under capacity constraints (owner: Runtime)
Incident playbook: Ensure runbook entries for throttling, elevated latency, model OOM, and catastrophic quality regressions are present and owners assigned (owner: SRE)
Archival: Tag model with deprecation window and lifecycle policy for future pruning (owner: PM)
Metrics alerting: Create automated alerts for p95 latency increases and error-rate spikes tied to the new model (owner: Observability)
Billing limits: Set sensible default rate limits and quota tiers for new model to prevent runaway cost during early adoption (owner: Billing)
Data handling: Document if inference logs are stored, retention period, and PII handling notes for Private customers (owner: Security/Privacy)
Monitoring smoke test: Execute a smoke checklist after publish: sample generation, streaming, function call, embedding, and SDK example (owner: Release Lead)
notes: Decision: Use quantized fp16 variant as default for hosted catalog listing based on benchmark trade-offs in ENG-4210.
Trade-off: Higher batch sizes reduced cost 18% but increased p95 by ~40ms on A100-40; we prefer p95 stability for latency-sensitive customers.
Blocker: Pending security review for third-party tokenizer license — blocker until 2025-03-08.
Follow-up: Add new eval prompts targeting instruction-following edge-cases in next cycle if regressions observed.
Owner note: Coordinate embargo time with Marketing; target public announcement 2025-03-20 16:00 UTC.
post_launch_metrics: Model quality regressions on evaluation suite
